decision.evidence: The binary policy checks 1218 consequences across 669 sites with 635 inconclusive sites. The largest regression, edit 40, spends 0.61726 cumulative profiled seconds transporting/checking supports (including 0.56672 RUP checking), versus 0.28442 compiling seven closures. Nested cumulative times overlap.
decision.limitation: Two alternating repetitions on exposed edits with provisioned origin banks. Native dispatch and gate counters do not bound total work or memory. Greater local closure does not establish a whole-query benefit; comparisons retain every regression.
decision.next_target: Build the tentative matching short-guard graph before transporting and RUP-checking every local consequence. A satisfiable superset graph rejects this closure opportunity; a contradictory graph requires checked supports on both witness paths before native source publication. Remove invalid edges and retry within a budget, or retain ordinary fallback. Compare with the eager gate, ordinary search and guided certificate reuse, including unsupported paths, misses and cold replay. A tentative empty clause needs its own checked local unit certificate.
decision.result: Supported short-guard interactions compile to checked native local closures: 25 with unit guards and 34 with binary guards on different live paths. All eight whole queries remain unresolved.
decision.scope: Keep tentative recognition separate from checked authority. Source-support containment, native unit/split recomposition, automatic origin discovery, wider guards, fresh unlabelled evaluation and uniformly efficient arbitrary-CNF closure remain explicit obligations.
decision.secondary_target: Sharing repeated exact core bodies in the separate hint bank remains open, but does not remove this gate preparation cost.
decision.status: experimental; both live gates regress; no default change

limitations: Both readers fully check one database per target/arm. The two repetitions have identical six-table payloads, counters and binary archive hashes within each arm. The frozen ordinary/certificate controls retain their prior payloads.

Every admitted guard is RUP-checked locally; both implication paths publish source-bound native unit/split evidence. The adapter has truth-table, transport, invalidation, exhausted-limit and live-routing tests, without a new Lean refinement proof.

Incremental cumulative audit: every old payload is byte-identical, new nodes/dependencies replay through both readers, and previous full-history/342-partition checks remain hash-bound rather than rerun.
Exposed inputs and provisioned banks remain limitations. No total work/memory cap or polynomial arbitrary-SAT expansion bound follows from native dispatch or gate allowances.

All eight exposed edits, with two alternating serial repetitions. Restore only each chronological origin prefix and its prior conditional support bank; no later repeat, cumulative union or posthoc hint archive seeds search.

Ordinary uses the frozen lazy binary closure solver. Certificate uses the frozen guided selector with direct trace reuse. Units and binary use ordinary fallback selection, exact source-coordinate tracking and a short-guard closure at ordinary probe sites. No distinct new tracking-only arm is measured.

Units checks zero/one-unfixed guards, opposite units first, then original binary clauses plus units. Binary also admits two-unfixed guards. The SCC result supplies only contradictions; both implication paths compile to native source unit/split certificates.

Budgets cap candidate checks, reserved support literals and compiled witness edges. They do not cap initial validation, guard-pair scans, native checking, total work, retained database size or process memory. The native 256-dispatch allowance excludes separately compiled proof nodes.

Worker time includes prefix restoration, setup, solve, new-node warm replay, full native cold replay, accounting, serialization and compression. Imports, frozen-source hashing and case loading are outside it. Earlier origin acquisition/extraction and final preservation audits remain additional.

Templates are explicitly provisioned and the population exposed. Whole-query completion, total cost and preservation must be measured; the preceding offline local savings do not establish a live gain or arbitrary-SAT bound.
